step1_analysis.circuit_type: RF Power Amplifier with Avalanche-Tolerant Bias Circuit
step1_analysis.description: An RF amplifier stage (Q2) equipped with a specialized active bias circuit designed to sink collector-base avalanche current. This allows the amplifier to operate at supply voltages exceeding the standard BVCEO limit by presenting a low DC impedance to the base of the RF transistor.

paper_reference.title: Analyses and Design of Bias Circuits Tolerating Output Voltages Above BVCEO

operating_frequency.description: The target frequency for the RF amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: Generic NPN models in standard SPICE can simulate at 1 GHz to 60 GHz, but accurate 60 GHz operation requires extracted parasitic models. We will test at 1 GHz for functional verification.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Paper reports 60 GHz to 130 GHz for SiGe. For a generic testbench, 1 GHz is used to verify AC gain.

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption of the bias circuit and PA stage.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly given, but efficiency is 50%

sky130_expected.calculation: I1=100uA, I2=100uA. Q4 sets 1*Vbe, mirrored to Q2. I_Q2 ≈ 100uA. Total current ≈ 300uA. Power = 1.8V * 300uA = 0.54mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the 100uA bias currents and 1:1 current mirroring to the PA stage.

voltage_gain.description: AC voltage gain from RF_in to PA_out.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gm of Q2 at 100uA is Ic/Vt = 100uA/26mV ≈ 3.8mS. With a 50 ohm load, gain = Gm * Rl = 3.8mS * 50 = 0.19 (-14 dB). To get positive gain, higher bias current (e.g., 5mA) is typically used in PAs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the chosen bias current and load impedance. The testbench uses 100uA for functional verification.

bias_voltage.description: DC voltage at the base of the RF transistor (N7).

sky130_expected.calculation: N8 is at 2*Vbe. Q3 drops 1*Vbe. N6 is at 1*Vbe. L1 is a DC short, so N7 is at 1*Vbe ≈ 0.7V to 0.8V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard forward-biased base-emitter voltage for a bipolar transistor.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to verify the DC bias point, AC voltage gain, and transient output swing of the avalanche-tolerant PA circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Avalanche-Tolerant Bias Circuit and PA Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Generic BJT models for functional verification
.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100)
.model pnp pnp (is=1e-16 bf=50)

* Parameters
.param I_bias=100u
.param L_val=1n
.param C_val=1p
.param VDD=1.8

* DUT
I1 VCC_bias N8 {I_bias}
I2 VCC_bias N0 {I_bias}
Q3 N0 N8 N6 npn
Q7 N1 N5 N0 pnp
Q2 N3 N7 GND npn
Q8 N6 N1 GND npn
Q4 N5 N5 GND npn
Q9 N8 N1 GND npn
Q1 N8 N8 N5 npn
C1 N3 PA_out {C_val}
C2 N7 RF_in {C_val}
L1 N6 N7 {L_val}
L2 N3 VCC_PA {L_val}

* Sources and Loads
V1 VCC_bias GND {VDD}
V2 VCC_PA GND {VDD}
Vrf RF_in GND dc 0 ac 1 sin(0 0.1 1G)
Rload PA_out GND 50

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point
op
let power = (-i(V1) - i(V2)) * 1.8
print power
print v(N6) v(N7)

* 2. AC Analysis
ac dec 20 100M 10G
let gain_db = vdb(PA_out)
meas ac max_gain max gain_db

* 3. Transient Analysis
tran 10p 5n
meas tran v_max max v(PA_out)
meas tran v_min min v(PA_out)

quit
.endc
.end
